prompt: Write a miniature dependency-injection container: given a Class, find its single constructor, build each parameter the same way, and instantiate it. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: This is the core trick behind real injection frameworks: instead of hard-coding `new RoadCar(new MotorUnit(), new WheelSet())`, the container reads the constructor signature at runtime and fills it in. getDeclaredConstructors plus getParameterTypes describe what a type needs, and the recursion supplies each need the same way, so the depth of the object graph costs nothing extra. Insisting on exactly one constructor keeps the rule unambiguous and gives a clear failure for types the container cannot handle. The unchecked cast to T is the usual price of turning a Class<T> back into a T.
hints: getDeclaredConstructors() returns an array. Reject anything whose length is not 1 before you touch it, using the exact message given in the Javadoc.
constructor.getParameterTypes() is a Class<?>[]. Build an Object[] of the same length and fill slot i by calling build on parameterTypes[i].
newInstance takes varargs, so passing your Object[] straight to constructor.newInstance(arguments) spreads it across the parameters. A zero-length array works fine for a no-argument constructor.
